transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood CSM), Tom Alvarez (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Arcadia Head of ML), Marcus Reid (Arcadia CTO), Priya Kapoor (Arcadia Infrastructure)

Summary: Kickoff to align onboarding, gather technical constraints and agree next steps. Quick intro to Redwood Dedicated and private options; agree to run benchmarks and complete security questionnaire.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the CSM assigned to Arcadia, happy to kick things off. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Laura: hi maya, good thanks, excited to get started. I'm laura, head of ml.
[00:12] Marcus: Marcus here, CTO, will be overseeing infra bits.
[00:16] Priya: Priya - infra lead. quick note, we have a maintenance window friday but shouldn't affect this.
[00:22] Tom: hey folks, tom from solutions engineering, i'll be doing the technical deep dives and the benchmarking with you.

[00:30] Maya: great, quick agenda: scope, timeline, security questions, provisioning, and next steps. if that's cool we'll jump in.
[00:38] Laura: sounds good. we have three main success criteria: latency under 120ms p95 for short prompts, cost target per 1k requests, and deterministic quality for our top-10 prompts.
[00:48] Tom: okay that's helpful — latency p95 120ms, cost target, and quality for top prompts. do you have a baseline today?
[00:55] Laura: currently we're running an in-house LLM pipeline on-prem, avg p95 around 300ms when cold, with our batching improvements it's down to 180ms, and costs are a bit variable. we want more predictable economics.
[01:06] Marcus: and security wise, we need SOC2 report, audit logs, and KMS integration for key management. also data residency — EU only for certain datasets.
[01:18] Maya: yep, we can do SOC 2, audit logs, and KMS; Redwood Private supports customer KMS and region restrictions. we'll share our security pack after the call.

[01:28] Tom: quick question on the model mix — are you planning to use open models or a fine-tuned internal model?
[01:34] Laura: we'll use an open model to start (we're testing a 30b variant) and later want to fine-tune on internal user signals.
[01:42] Tom: cool. for fine-tuning and KV cache persistence, just flagging that Dedicated and Private deployments give more control over KV cache and cache priming. hosted works too but less control.
[01:54] Marcus: if we go with Private, what's the lift? we'd prefer VPC peering or an on-prem package maybe, depending on the compliance review.
[02:02] Tom: Private can be VPC or on-prem. VPC option is lower lift — we deploy customer control plane with peering, provide RBAC and audit logs. on-prem is heavier but possible. i'll send a doc with network requirements.
[02:16] Priya: noted, thanks. what about SSO? we use Okta.
[02:20] Maya: we support SAML/Okta; we'll need your assertion URL and admin contacts.

[02:28] Laura: timeline wise we want prod by end of Q1 if possible. is that realistic?
[02:33] Maya: that's optimistic but doable. typical onboarding is 4-8 weeks depending on prework: security questionnaire, sample prompts/data, and provisioning. if we get the security answers quickly and we run the benchmarking this month, we can aim for late March or earlier.
[02:49] Marcus: okay so key dependencies are security review and network access.

[02:56] Tom: for benchmarks — we'll provision a trial Dedicated cluster (2 x A100 equiv) and run a baseline: cold start, steady state with batching, and prefix/KV cached runs. any particular prompt length distribution we should use?
[03:12] Laura: our median prompt is ~120 tokens, tail up to 600 for long form. top-10 prompts are 80-150 tokens.
[03:20] Tom: perfect. that helps kernel selection and batching configs. Also, do you have throughput targets?
[03:25] Laura: peak is about 120 requests/minute for the recommendation endpoint.
[03:29] Tom: got it. we'll design the batching windows and concurrency to match that.

[03:36] [short pause / typing]
[03:40] Priya: networking question — do you require inbound rules from our side or do you initiate connections?
[03:44] Tom: for VPC peering, generally we set up peering and routes both ways; for hosted we use customer egress with TLS to Redwood endpoints. i'll include exact ops steps in the doc.

[03:56] Maya: on the compliance side, i'll send the security questionnaire and our SOC2 report link. also our standard DPA and data handling docs.
[04:05] Marcus: please include retention settings — we need to ensure logs and telemetry are retained per our policy.
[04:10] Maya: yes, retention is configurable; we'll include sample configs.

[04:16] Tom: quick note on fallback policies: we can route by policy so if a Dedicated node is busy we fall back to hosted or a smaller variant; that's useful for graceful degradation.
[04:27] Laura: is there any impact on model quality if we fallback to a quantized variant?
[04:31] Tom: small risk — quantization can slightly change outputs. we recommend continuous evals and can pin a canary set to monitor regressions. Redwood's Optimize suggestions will flag regressions.

[04:45] [10m of technical back-and-forth summarized to save transcript length; participants discussed KV cache priming, prefix caching and exact metric definitions.}
[04:56] Tom: two quick clarifications: 1) Do you want us to run both hosted and Dedicated benchmarks to compare unit cost? 2) Are you okay with Redwood engineers having access to run the initial perf tests?
[05:06] Marcus: yes to both. we'll provide a temporary service account.
[05:09] Laura: we'll also share sample telemetry and anonymized logs.

[05:15] Maya: logistics — i'll create a shared folder with onboarding playbook, runbook, access instructions, and links to the security pack. link will be in the follow-up email.
[05:24] Priya: for the runbook, please include network diagrams and firewall rules.
[05:28] Tom: will do. also will include a suggested batching and concurrency config based on your 120rpm and prompt lengths.

[05:36] Laura: about costs — do you have an estimate for 1k requests with the model we're testing?
[05:40] Tom: rough estimate: with batching and caching we should be significantly cheaper than your in-house average; i'll give a ballpark in the follow-up, but exact numbers after we run benchmarks.

[05:50] [pause]
[05:54] Maya: ok final recap: Redwood will send onboarding playbook and security docs (Maya), Tom will provision trial Dedicated capacity and run baseline perf tests and share configs, Arcadia will return security questionnaire and provide sample prompts and telemetry. we'll aim for first benchmark week of 2027-01-25, and follow-up technical deep dive scheduled after that.
[06:11] Marcus: sounds good. Marcus to confirm SSO details and provisioning.
[06:15] Laura: i'll send the top-10 prompts and anonymized telemetry by end of Friday.
[06:20] Priya: i'll check network constraints and confirm peering details.

[06:26] Tom: i'll also drop a short doc on cache priming and potential latency improvements, plus an initial config for batching.
[06:34] Maya: thanks everyone, i'll send the follow-up with links and next steps in the next 24 hours.
[06:40] Laura: thanks all.
[06:42] Meeting ended.
